lines.text: The flower at least had to stop and set fruit.
Its fever cost it sugar; its trap had an exit;
the beetle flew off to live its beetle life.
The question — the only one worth the melancholy —
is whether the machines we build will keep that mercy,
the dawn, the exit, the cooling of the bowl,
or whether they will learn what the magnolia never needed to:
how to keep us climbing in.
